BBC — full candidate list, Holborn and St Pancras by-election

BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountNotificationsHomeNewsSportWeatheriPlayerSoundsBitesizeCBBCCBeebiesFoodMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportWeatheriPlayerSoundsBitesizeCBBCCBeebiesFoodClose menuBBC NewsMenuHomeUKWorldBusinessCulturePoliticsHealthTechInDepthBBC VerifyClimateMoreScienceFamily & EducationIn PicturesDisabilityNewsbeatEnglandLocal NewsLondonWho are the candidates in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election?Image source, EPAImage caption, The Holborn and St Pancras by-election is set to take place on 8 October
The candidates have been announced who will stand in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, which is set to take place on 8 October.
The seat became vacant after former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer announced he was standing down to focus on a role in international affairs.
Here are the people who have announced they are standing to become the area's next MP, listed in alphabetical order.
Nominations closed on Tuesday 15 September at 16:00 BST. Camden Council has since published its full list of named candidates.
Some candidates formally confirmed by the council have not yet released biographical details or campaign platforms. This article will be updated as further information and official statements become available.
Sagal Abdi-Wali - Labour Party
Image source, LabourImage caption, Sagal Abdi-Wali has been selected as the Labour Party candidate
Camden Council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali is standing for the Labour Party.
She has led the local authority since May, having been a councillor for Camden Square since 2022.
Camden leader to stand for Keir Starmer's old seat
Barmy Brunch - Official Monster Raving Loony Party
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Barmy Brunch is the Official Monster Raving Loony Party candidate
Barmy Brunch, a "clown" standing as an MP in a baked bean mask, is the Official Monster Raving Loony Party candidate.
Ewan Cameron - Conservatives
Image source, ConservativesImage caption, Ewan Cameron has been selected as the Conservative candidate
Conservative member Ewan Cameron is standing for the Conservatives.
Cameron was a councillor on Camden Council from 1998 to 2002. During that time, he was vice-chair for licensing and a lead member on the development control committee.
Tories pick ex-councillor to contest Starmer's former seat
Tom Darwood - Independent
Image source, Tom Darwood/YouTubeImage caption, Tom Darwood is an independent candidate
Tom Darwood is a former carpenter who said his family fled from Communist-controlled China in 1954.
Clare Fischer - Climate Party
Image source, Climate PartyImage caption, Clare Fischer is contesting the seat for the Climate Party
The Climate Party has selected Clare Fischer to stand in the October by-election.
Fischer trained as an actress before changing careers to run a music venue in Highgate for the past 20 years.
She first became involved with the party in recent weeks, but has long-held concerns over climate change.
George Galloway - Workers Party
Image source, UK ParliamentImage caption, George Galloway is standing for the Workers Party
George Galloway, leader of the Workers Party of Britain, will contest the seat for the party.
Galloway has been leader of the Workers Party since he founded it in 2019, and is a former leader of the Respect Party.
He has served as a Member of Parliament seven times for five different constituencies.
Tyler Johnson - Restore Britain
Image source, RestoreImage caption, Tyler Johnson has been selected as the Restore Britain candidate
Tyler Johnson has been selected as the Restore Britain candidate.
He is a corporate lawyer based in London.
Briony Kapoor - Rejoin EU Party
Image source, Rejoin EU PartyImage caption, Briony Kapoor is the candidate for the Rejoin EU Party
Briony Kapoor will stand as a candidate for the Rejoin EU Party in the by-election.
Kapoor previously served two terms as an independent town councillor in Folkestone and Hythe.
Pete Newman - Reform UK
Image source, Reform UKImage caption, Pete Newman has been selected as the Reform UK candidate
Pete Newman will stand as the candidate for Reform UK in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election on 8 October.
He served with the Metropolitan Police between 2004 and 2009 as a senior detective, working on crime reduction and counter-terrorism across London.
Ex-Met detective to stand for Reform in by-election
Ketankumar Pipaliya - UK VOICE safer and stronger UK
Image source, Ketankumar Pipaliya/InstagramImage caption, Ketankumar Pipaliya is the UK VOICE candidate
Ketankumar Pipaliya has run in several parliamentary constituencies for the UK VOICE party. He has been described as a pharmaceuticals entrepreneur.
Zack Polanski - Green Party
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Zack Polanski has been selected as the Green Party candidate
Zack Polanski has been leader of the Green Party of England and Wales since September 2025 and a member of the London Assembly since May 2021.
He was the deputy leader of the Greens from 2022 to 2025.
Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat
Jonathan Silberman - Communist League
Image source, Jonathan SilbermanImage caption, Jonathan Silberman is the Communist League candidate
Jonathan Silberman has previously announced runs for mayor of London and contested parliamentary elections for the Communist League. He organised strike action during a long career as a shop-floor worker in the manufacturing industries.
Helen Spiby-Vann - Christian Peoples Alliance
Image source, Helen Spiby-VannImage caption, Helen Spiby-Vann will contest the seat for the Christian Peoples Alliance
The Christian Peoples Alliance has selected Helen Spiby-Vann to stand as its candidate.
Spiby-Vann is a self-employed graphic designer who lives in Finsbury Park.
Patrick Stillman - Liberal Democrats
Image source, Liberal DemocratsImage caption, Patrick Stillman has been selected as the Lib Dem candidate
Patrick Stillman, Lib Dem councillor for West Hampstead, is standing for the Liberal Democrats.
Stillman is also the outgoing chairman of Camden Liberal Democrats.
Lib Dem councillor to contest Starmer's seat.
Ben Walker - UK Independence Party (UKIP)
Image source, UKIPImage caption, Ben Walker is the UKIP candidate
Ben Walker is national party chairman of UKIP. The party's website says he is a Navy veteran and former county councillor, local authority vice chair and town mayor.
